summary: Fix bbb78fd closes the fix_task: all three AC-6/AC-7 sites now distinguish auxiliary-run failure from a real negative before registrar_ok. Prior confirmations undisturbed.
notes: contract-check ok=true; not_checked: forbid.behaviors (verified by hand: fix commit bbb78fd touches only deploy/verificar_aislamiento.sh, no other file; commit message is Spanish, conventional-commit style, no AI attribution line).

Fix_task hex-076-live-script-distinguish-tool-failure verified CLOSED by reading git show bbb78fd (not the implementer's claim alone): a new fallo_de_auxiliar() checks CODIGO_AUXILIAR (exit 125) or ERR_AUXILIAR ('Error response from daemon' stderr match), and desde()/leer_volumen()/escribir_volumen() now capture both via 2>"$ERR_TEMP" plus an explicit CODIGO_AUXILIAR=$? before returning. All three flagged call sites (AC-6 read: elif fallo_de_auxiliar after the desde() cross-read check; AC-6 write: elif fallo_de_auxiliar after the leer_volumen() cross-write check; AC-7 loop: elif fallo_de_auxiliar after each desde()/nc reach check) place the new elif branch strictly before the final else registrar_ok, so a broken auxiliary can no longer fall through to a false 'OK: aislado'. Each new FALLA message names which vector/probe could not be tested and includes the exit code.

No staleness across probes: CODIGO_AUXILIAR/ERR_AUXILIAR are unconditionally overwritten on every desde()/leer_volumen()/escribir_volumen() call, and all three fix-site checks read the globals immediately after the single relevant call with no intervening call in between (confirmed by reading the surrounding if/elif chains and the AC-7 for-loop body). ERR_TEMP is added to the EXIT trap's rm -f alongside the pre-existing ENV_TEMP_A/B, so no new leaked temp file.

Pre-existing precondition branches (escribir_volumen(B,...) for the read vector, desde(A, echo...) for the write vector) already collapsed tool-failure and command-failure into the same safe 'no se pudo probar' message before this fix and still do; the fix only had to add the new elif to the second call in each chain, which is exactly what it did.

Residual, out of this fix_task's scope and NOT introduced by bbb78fd: AC-8's socket-device comparison calls desde()/leer_volumen() inside command substitution ($(...)), which runs in a subshell -- CODIGO_AUXILIAR/ERR_AUXILIAR set there never reach the parent shell, but AC-8 doesn't consult those globals (it relies on the containerized command's own 'stat ... || echo NOEXISTE' fallback for stdout). A docker-run-level failure during that retry loop would produce empty stdout rather than the literal string NOEXISTE, which the current retry/compare logic does not special-case, and could in principle print an incorrect 'OK: son objetos de archivo distintos'. This is pre-existing code untouched by the diff under review, was implicitly accepted by the first review pass, requires a rare docker-run failure mid-script (alpine:3 already pulled by then), and the script remains human-run with acceptance.human_gate: true before merge -- flagged here for awareness, not as a new blocking fix_task.

All items the first review already confirmed (contract-check clean, AC-1..AC-11 coverage, D-48 logged correctly, static guard's mutation self-test non-vacuous, attacker-fidelity of --network container:<target>/--volumes-from, live script correctly excluded from CI/verify.commands) are undisturbed: bbb78fd touches only deploy/verificar_aislamiento.sh and does not touch deploy/verificar_aislamiento_estatica.sh, docs/bitacora-de-descartes.md, .github/workflows/ci.yml, README.md, or docs/plan/fase-a-6-empaquetado-cli.md (those five files' content is identical to what the first review already reviewed under the prior commit f2205af).
05-validation.json (executed_at 2026-09-13T22:23:57Z) shows all seven verify.commands re-run after the fix, all exit 0, including the --autoprueba mutation self-test at 3/3.

The live script's two-cell cross-container behavior, including the new fallo_de_auxiliar() classifier itself, has still never been exercised end-to-end against real running containers within this task's trace -- deliberately deferred per contract design (touch/forbid.behaviors bars wiring it into CI or verify.commands) and covered by acceptance.human_gate: true; this is a human-gated precondition to merge, not a defect to loop on.
